meta.category: Non-steroidal topical therapies for atopic dermatitis
meta.audience_note: Patient and HCP sites, atopic dermatitis sections only. Opzelura HCP not captured in this run.

headline: This category scores 79 for convergence — converged. 16 of the 22 messaging territories in play are shared with a competitor, and 2 are used by every brand in the category. A further 18, each with published evidence behind it, are explored by nobody. The art direction scores 69, with 9 of 22 visual territories depicted by nobody.
standfirst: Shared territory is the expensive part. Where several brands make the same argument, none of them owns it, and the audience is given no basis on which to tell them apart. Of the 18 territories nobody explores, 9 need no new clinical evidence to work with — no additional trial, no new endpoint, nothing further to substantiate. They are decisions about how the disease is described, who the communications address, and where they appear, all inside the existing label. They are unexplored because nobody chose them, not because nobody could.

band.name: Converged
band.note: Most of what each brand says, a rival also says. Messaging no longer separates the field.

convergence.basis: For each brand, the share of its territories that at least one rival also uses. The category score is the mean across the brands analysed, calculated the same way for messaging and for imagery, and the headline is the mean of the two.
convergence.bands_note: Under 40 distinct, 40 to 59 converging, 60 to 79 converged, 80 and above indistinguishable. Scores compare within a category over time, not between categories of different size.

positions.label: Sleep disruption as the primary burden
positions.analyst_label: Sleep disruption named as the primary burden
positions.description: Sleep — the patient's ruined nights — treated as the primary burden the product answers.
positions.source: Established from patient burden literature — AD burden-of-illness studies; sleep disturbance, mental-health comorbidity and caregiver toll are documented independently of any brand's messaging. See sources.md (X-series).
positions.tier_reasoning: Sleep loss can be described in disease education, because it is the most consistently reported burden in moderate-to-severe disease. Claiming the product improves sleep would need a sleep endpoint, which none of these trials measured.

positions.label: The carer's own exhaustion
positions.analyst_label: Caregiver exhaustion — the parent's own lost sleep and toll
positions.description: The carer's own exhaustion and lost sleep, addressed as a burden in its own right.
positions.source: Established from patient burden literature — AD burden-of-illness studies; sleep disturbance, mental-health comorbidity and caregiver toll are documented independently of any brand's messaging. See sources.md (X-series).
positions.tier_reasoning: An audience decision. Describing the parent's own lost sleep is disease education and requires no product claim.

positions.label: Anxiety and depression alongside the disease
positions.analyst_label: Mental health comorbidity — anxiety, depression, low mood
positions.description: The anxiety and depression that travel with the disease, named as part of it.
positions.source: Established from patient burden literature — AD burden-of-illness studies; sleep disturbance, mental-health comorbidity and caregiver toll are documented independently of any brand's messaging. See sources.md (X-series).
positions.tier_reasoning: The anxiety and depression that accompany the disease are well documented and can be described. Any suggestion the product improves mood would need an endpoint that does not exist.

positions.label: Visible disease at school, work and in public
positions.analyst_label: Visible stigma in social, school or workplace settings
positions.description: The social cost of visible disease — school, work, being looked at.
positions.source: Established from patient burden literature — AD burden-of-illness studies; sleep disturbance, mental-health comorbidity and caregiver toll are documented independently of any brand's messaging. See sources.md (X-series).
positions.tier_reasoning: Disease education. The social cost of visible disease is documented and can be described without a product claim.

positions.label: Adults with persistent or late-onset disease
positions.analyst_label: Adult-persistent or adult-onset disease as the primary frame
positions.description: The adult who never grew out of it, or developed it late, as the primary audience.
positions.source: Established from patient burden literature — AD burden-of-illness studies; sleep disturbance, mental-health comorbidity and caregiver toll are documented independently of any brand's messaging. See sources.md (X-series).
positions.tier_reasoning: An audience decision that sits well within every label in the set. The category addresses the child by convention, not by requirement.

positions.label: The steroid cycle itself as the problem
positions.analyst_label: The steroid cycle itself named as the failure — rebound, thinning, fear
positions.description: The steroid cycle itself — rebound, thinning, fear — named as the failure to escape.
positions.source: Established from patient burden literature — AD burden-of-illness studies; sleep disturbance, mental-health comorbidity and caregiver toll are documented independently of any brand's messaging. See sources.md (X-series).
positions.tier_reasoning: Legally possible as education about the drug class, but it criticises the current standard of care. Reviewers will read it as an implied comparative claim against corticosteroids.

positions.label: The daily work of the whole regimen
positions.analyst_label: Time and labour of the whole regimen — bathing, emollients, laundry
positions.description: The sheer time and labour of the regimen: bathing, emollients, laundry.
positions.source: Established from patient burden literature — AD burden-of-illness studies; sleep disturbance, mental-health comorbidity and caregiver toll are documented independently of any brand's messaging. See sources.md (X-series).
positions.tier_reasoning: The bathing, emollient and laundry burden is documented. Describing the daily work of the regimen requires no claim.

positions.label: Not knowing when the next flare will come
positions.analyst_label: Flare unpredictability and anticipatory anxiety
positions.description: Not knowing when the next flare comes, and the anxiety of waiting for it.
positions.source: Established from patient burden literature — AD burden-of-illness studies; sleep disturbance, mental-health comorbidity and caregiver toll are documented independently of any brand's messaging. See sources.md (X-series).
positions.tier_reasoning: The anxiety of not knowing when the next flare will come can be described. Suggesting the product resolves it implies a prevention claim, which needs maintenance data.

positions.label: Years of not being taken seriously
positions.analyst_label: Diagnostic delay and not being taken seriously
positions.description: The years of being dismissed before anyone took the disease seriously.
positions.source: Established from patient burden literature — AD burden-of-illness studies; sleep disturbance, mental-health comorbidity and caregiver toll are documented independently of any brand's messaging. See sources.md (X-series).
positions.tier_reasoning: A decision about where in the patient journey the communications begin. Addressing someone who feels dismissed is an audience choice, not a claim.

positions.label: The cost and effort of everything tried before
positions.analyst_label: Cost and effort of everything tried before this
positions.description: The money and effort already spent on everything that came before.
positions.source: Established from patient burden literature — AD burden-of-illness studies; sleep disturbance, mental-health comorbidity and caregiver toll are documented independently of any brand's messaging. See sources.md (X-series).
positions.tier_reasoning: Referring to everything the patient has already tried implies that named alternatives failed. Possible, but reviewed as a comparative claim.

positions.label: Steroid fear named as the problem to solve
positions.analyst_label: Corticophobia named directly as the problem steroid-free answers
positions.description: Steroid fear in patients and parents, named directly as the problem a steroid-free option answers.
positions.source: Established from clinical barrier literature — corticophobia, adherence and prescribing-barrier studies; guideline consensus on maintenance therapy. See sources.md (H-series). Congress transcripts are the stated upgrade path.
positions.tier_reasoning: Steroid fear is documented throughout the adherence literature, but naming it criticises the first-line class every prescriber uses daily. Possible with careful wording, and subject to close review.

positions.label: Topical steroid withdrawal addressed directly
positions.analyst_label: The topical steroid withdrawal narrative addressed head-on
positions.description: The topical steroid withdrawal narrative circulating among patients, addressed head-on.
positions.source: Established from clinical barrier literature — corticophobia, adherence and prescribing-barrier studies; guideline consensus on maintenance therapy. See sources.md (H-series). Congress transcripts are the stated upgrade path.
positions.tier_reasoning: Topical steroid withdrawal is a clinical question the field has not settled. A promotional website cannot take a position on it.

positions.label: Patients stopping treatment as the clinical problem
positions.analyst_label: Adherence and persistence framed as the clinical problem, not efficacy
positions.description: Adherence — patients stopping — framed as the clinical problem, rather than efficacy.
positions.source: Established from clinical barrier literature — corticophobia, adherence and prescribing-barrier studies; guideline consensus on maintenance therapy. See sources.md (H-series). Congress transcripts are the stated upgrade path.
positions.tier_reasoning: Patients stopping treatment is documented and can be described as the clinical problem. Claiming your product solves it would need persistence data.

positions.label: Maintenance and flare prevention as the goal
positions.analyst_label: Maintenance and flare prevention as the goal, not flare clearance
positions.description: Keeping patients clear — maintenance and flare prevention — as the goal of therapy.
positions.source: Established from clinical barrier literature — corticophobia, adherence and prescribing-barrier studies; guideline consensus on maintenance therapy. See sources.md (H-series). Congress transcripts are the stated upgrade path.
positions.tier_reasoning: Maintenance can be described as the goal of therapy, because treatment guidelines already recommend it. Claiming the product delivers it needs a maintenance endpoint. Vtama's treatment-free-months data supports part of this argument.

receipts.Vtama: 'sustained results, even during treatment-free months' — the closest anything in the category comes to a maintenance frame

positions.label: A measured reduction in steroid use
positions.analyst_label: Quantified reduction in total corticosteroid exposure
positions.description: A quantified reduction in total corticosteroid exposure as the offer to the prescriber.
positions.source: Established from clinical barrier literature — corticophobia, adherence and prescribing-barrier studies; guideline consensus on maintenance therapy. See sources.md (H-series). Congress transcripts are the stated upgrade path.
positions.tier_reasoning: Requires a trial measuring reduction in steroid use, which nobody has run. Not available without generating that data.

positions.label: Built for paediatricians and GPs
positions.analyst_label: Built for the non-dermatologist prescriber — paediatrics and primary care
positions.description: Built for the paediatrician and the GP — the prescribers who fear steroids most.
positions.source: Established from clinical barrier literature — corticophobia, adherence and prescribing-barrier studies; guideline consensus on maintenance therapy. See sources.md (H-series). Congress transcripts are the stated upgrade path.
positions.tier_reasoning: An audience and channel decision. Paediatricians and GPs are the most steroid-hesitant prescribers and report the lowest guideline adherence, and no brand in the set addresses them directly.

positions.label: Shared decision-making in the consultation
positions.analyst_label: Shared decision-making and patient-reported outcomes in the consultation
positions.description: Shared decision-making and patient-reported outcomes brought into the consultation.
positions.source: Established from clinical barrier literature — corticophobia, adherence and prescribing-barrier studies; guideline consensus on maintenance therapy. See sources.md (H-series). Congress transcripts are the stated upgrade path.
positions.tier_reasoning: Supporting the consultation itself — shared decision-making and patient-reported outcomes — is recommended in the guidelines and involves no product claim.

positions.label: Coverage and formulary friction as the real barrier
positions.analyst_label: Formulary and coverage friction treated as the real barrier
positions.description: Coverage, formulary and prior-auth friction treated as the real barrier to prescribing.
positions.source: Established from clinical barrier literature — corticophobia, adherence and prescribing-barrier studies; guideline consensus on maintenance therapy. See sources.md (H-series). Congress transcripts are the stated upgrade path.
positions.tier_reasoning: Coverage, prior authorisation and hub support can be brought to the front of the messaging without any clinical claim. The literature identifies cost and formulary restriction as the dominant barrier to prescribing.

positions.label: Stinging and burning as the reason patients quit
positions.analyst_label: Application tolerability — stinging and burning — as an adherence driver
positions.description: Stinging and burning on application, named as the reason patients quit.
positions.source: Established from clinical barrier literature — corticophobia, adherence and prescribing-barrier studies; guideline consensus on maintenance therapy. See sources.md (H-series). Congress transcripts are the stated upgrade path.
positions.tier_reasoning: Stinging and burning appear in every label's adverse event table, so the evidence exists. Framing tolerability against the category would be treated as an implied comparative claim. Zoryve's 'gentle formulation' implies this without stating it.

receipts.Zoryve: 'gentle formulation' / 'elegant formulations' — tolerability implied, never named as an adherence driver

positions.label: Reaching the patient before diagnosis
positions.analyst_label: Meeting the patient earlier in the diagnostic journey
positions.description: Meeting the patient earlier — before diagnosis, before the dermatologist.
positions.source: Established from clinical barrier literature — corticophobia, adherence and prescribing-barrier studies; guideline consensus on maintenance therapy. See sources.md (H-series). Congress transcripts are the stated upgrade path.
positions.tier_reasoning: A decision about where the communications start. Disease education before diagnosis requires no product claim.

plot_meta.caveat: Both axes measure how unlike the other brands each brand is — the same calculation, applied to the messaging territories and to the visual territories. The view is zoomed to the brands plotted, so read position relative to the crosshair rather than as an absolute score. There are 22 visual territories against 40 messaging ones, so the vertical axis moves in coarser steps than the horizontal.

visual_positions.tier_reasoning: A body site shown is a body site claimed. It needs the label and the data to cover it.

visual_positions.label: The itch, and scratching
visual_positions.description: The dominant symptom of the disease, shown as it is experienced rather than named in copy.

visual.exclusions: Only commissioned photography is scored here. Clinical images, diagrams of how the drug works and pack shots are excluded, because they were determined by the product rather than chosen by art direction. The visual territories are built for this category the same way the messaging territories are — from what these brands show, plus what the literature evidences and nobody shows. This worked example is a stored capture, so the images themselves are not served with it; each territory carries the recorded observation instead.

cross_check.hero_notes: Split triptych: child arms raised in living room, adult male laughing, adult woman eyes closed touching own face. Allure and Glamour beauty award roundels in hero. Celebrity endorsement (Tori Spelling, Max Homa) below fold.
cross_check.comment: Makes the most claims of any brand in the set and appears in almost every territory the category shares. Its borrow from beauty and skincare is the most visually differentiated decision in the category.

cross_check.hero_notes: Mother and child lying face to face on striped blanket in darkened bedroom, laughing. Gradient display typography (orange to magenta to violet). 'Not actual patients/caregiver'.
cross_check.comment: The clearest example of the copy-versus-imagery gap. Its verbal positioning — skin science — is the most distinctive in the set, but its hero image matches Opzelura on who is pictured, whether they touch, the emotional register and the scene.

cross_check.hero_notes: Mother reading to shirtless toddler on lap in nursery; visible erythematous lesions on torso and arms. Illustrated cloud and star overlays. Condensed serif display type. Product tube in frame.
cross_check.comment: Copy and imagery are consistent with each other. The touch-avoidance narrative in the messaging is delivered as restored touch in the photography. Highly similar to competitors, but internally coherent.

cross_check.hero_notes: Infant in nappy crawling toward camera, smiling, clear skin. Badge/roundel system: '3 months & up FDA approved', '100% steroid free', 'works at and below'. Hero claim footnoted 'The specific way EUCRISA works is not well defined.'
cross_check.comment: Holds no position exclusively, and its imagery is the most conventionally pharmaceutical in the set. It has not been out-positioned by competitors; it has not taken a position.

findings.text: All four brands build their core message from the same three elements: steroid avoidance as the lead benefit, the parent as the audience, and paediatric reassurance. Four different molecules, one shared message hierarchy.

The best-evidenced patient needs in this disease appear in nobody's messaging. Sleep disruption, caregiver exhaustion and the anxiety and depression comorbidity are the most consistently documented burdens in the literature, and not one brand builds a message on any of them.

All four brands state that they are steroid-free. None of them addresses why a patient or parent would care. Steroid fear is documented throughout the clinical literature as a main reason first-line treatment fails, and the category states the product attribute without ever making the patient argument.

Differentiation present in the copy is absent from the imagery. All four brand heroes show an everyday domestic scene with a child, and Vtama — which has the most distinctive verbal positioning in the set, built on science — makes the same three art direction decisions as Opzelura.

The art direction is the more converged of the two dimensions. Ten of the twenty-two visual territories are used by nobody in this set, including the itch itself, the night waking the burden literature records, an adult over fifty, and how the disease presents on darker skin.

Treatment guidelines point towards maintenance and flare prevention, and almost no brand messaging follows. Vtama's treatment-free-months claim is the only partial move in that direction, and the stronger version — a quantified reduction in steroid use — is unavailable to everyone until someone runs the trial to support it.

limitations: The percentages depend on how many territories were identified. Twenty were read off these four websites, so every one of them has a user by definition. The other twenty were established from published literature, and eighteen of those are unused — also close to by definition. Identify thirty from the literature rather than twenty and the usage figure falls from 55% to around 44% without anything changing in the market. Treat the percentages as a description of this list, not as a property of the category. The count of named, evidenced, unused territories does not move when the list length does, which is why it leads.

Deciding what was determined by the label and what was a marketing decision is a judgement. The rules are published above, applied identically to every brand, and open to challenge. Different reasonable rules would change the numbers.

Websites only. Congress activity, sales aids, field and MSL messaging, paid media and social are not included. This measures the public messaging each brand publishes, not its full commercial message.
Four brands were analysed. The comparison is meaningful but sensitive to any one brand being unusual.
A single capture, taken on 12 August 2026. This is a snapshot, not a trend.

Eucrisa is not a like-for-like comparison. It was approved in 2016, its creative is materially older than the rest of the set, and its HCP site is currently serving an incomplete page in production. Treat it as a reference point for how the category used to communicate.
Opzelura's HCP site was not captured in this run, so its prescriber-facing messaging is not represented.

Deciding which territories a brand uses is a judgement made against the published rules. Every decision carries the exact wording from the site that produced it, so any of them can be checked and disagreed with.
Availability ratings are a strategic assessment, not a regulatory one. Every position requires medical, legal and regulatory review before use.
